Build a dashboard from a configuration

Source: R/dashconfig.R
rvisDashboard.Rd

Creates a DASHBOARD object from a configuration given as a YAML or JSON file, or as an R list. A configuration has these fields (only items and layout are required):

name

Name of the dashboard.

items

Named list of the dashboard items. Each item has a type (an input, output or container type) and the settings of that type. Output items have a service: R code returning the content of the output. Input items can have a service: R code run when the input changes.

layout

Name(s) of the item(s) making the page, usually a single page container like fluidPage, dashboardPage or navbarPage.

objects

Named list of objects copied into session$userData of each session.

values

Named list of initial values of the reactive list sync of each session.

prescript

R code run at the start of each session (for example to define reactive expressions).

observers

R code (one text per observer) run in observe() in each session.

settings, messages, loginTable

Settings, messages and users of dashboards with a login item.

The type of an item (or of its cloth) can also be any function of any package, written as package::function, like shinyWidgets::pickerInput or shinydashboard::box. The item fields are then passed to that function as they are, with the argument names of the package documentation. Functions with argument inputId make inputs and functions with argument outputId make outputs (the item name is passed as the id); all other functions are containers and get the items of their layout as unnamed arguments. A few fields are used by rvis and not passed to the function: args (unnamed arguments passed first, like the text of shiny::h3), service, layout, cloth, role (input, output or container, if the detected role is wrong), render (render function of an output, by default the package's renderFoo for output fooOutput), render.args (arguments of the render function), update (function used by updateItem(), by default the package's updateFoo for input foo) and the tooltip, popover and tutor fields. See rvisDashboardExample("generic-types").

Usage

rvisDashboard(config, ...)

Arguments

config

Path of a YAML (.yml, .yaml) or JSON (.json) file, or a list.

...

Configuration fields added to (or replacing those of) config, for example objects = list(data = mydata).

Value

A DASHBOARD object. Run it with $run() or get the shiny app with $app().

Details

In YAML files, values tagged !expr are R expressions evaluated when the file is read (for example choices: !expr names(mtcars)). Only true and false are read as logical values (words like yes, no, y or n stay text).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dash = rvisDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("hello"))
dash$run()

# from a list:
dash = rvisDashboard(list(
  layout = "page",
  items  = list(
    page = list(type = "fluidPage", title = "Hello", layout = list("n", "hist")),
    n    = list(type = "sliderInput", title = "Observations", min = 10, max = 500, value = 100),
    hist = list(type = "plotOutput", service = "hist(rnorm(input$n))"))))
shiny::runApp(dash$app())
} # }
